title: Edit Distance
prompt: Write a Python function `min_distance(word1: str, word2: str) -> int` that returns the minimum number of operations (insert, delete, or replace one character) required to convert `word1` into `word2`.

title: Regular Expression Matching
prompt: Write a Python function `is_match(s: str, p: str) -> bool` that implements regular expression matching with support for '.' (matches any single character) and '*' (matches zero or more of the preceding element). The matching must cover the entire input string `s`.

title: N-Queens Count
prompt: Write a Python function `total_n_queens(n: int) -> int` that returns the number of distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle: place `n` queens on an `n x n` chessboard so that no two queens attack each other.

title: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequences
prompt: Write a Python function `find_number_of_lis(nums: list[int]) -> int` that returns the number of longest increasing subsequences in `nums`. Return 0 if `nums` is empty.

title: Word Ladder Length
prompt: Write a Python function `ladder_length(begin_word: str, end_word: str, word_list: list[str]) -> int` that returns the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from `begin_word` to `end_word`, changing exactly one letter at a time, where every intermediate word must be in `word_list`. Return 0 if no such sequence exists. The count includes both `begin_word` and `end_word`.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
prompt: Write a Python function `max_sliding_window(nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]` that returns the maximum of each sliding window of size `k` as it moves from left to right. Return an empty list if `nums` is empty.

title: Course Schedule II (Valid Order)
prompt: Write a Python function `find_order(num_courses: int, prerequisites: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]` that returns any valid order in which all courses can be taken. Each prerequisite `[a, b]` means course `b` must be taken before course `a`. Return an empty list if no valid order exists (a cycle).
test_cases: pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(order)}
return all(pos[b] < pos[a] for a, b in pre)

title: Find Median from Data Stream
prompt: Implement a class `MedianFinder` in Python with methods `add_num(num: int) -> None` (adds a number to the data stream) and `find_median() -> float` (returns the median of all numbers added so far). `find_median` is only called when at least one number has been added.
test_cases: m = MedianFinder(); m.add_num(1); m.add_num(2); assert m.find_median() == 1.5
m = MedianFinder(); m.add_num(1); m.add_num(2); m.add_num(3); assert m.find_median() == 2.0
m = MedianFinder(); m.add_num(-1); m.add_num(-2); assert m.find_median() == -1.5
m = MedianFinder(); [m.add_num(x) for x in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]]; assert m.find_median() == 3.0
m = MedianFinder(); m.add_num(5); assert m.find_median() == 5.0; m.add_num(5); assert m.find_median() == 5.0
m = MedianFinder(); [m.add_num(x) for x in [10, 0, 5, 5]]; assert m.find_median() == 5.0

title: Next Permutation
prompt: Write a Python function `next_permutation(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]` that returns the next lexicographically greater permutation of `nums` as a new list (the input list must not be modified). If no greater permutation exists, return the smallest permutation (sorted ascending).

title: 3Sum
prompt: Write a Python function `three_sum(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]` that returns all unique triplets `[a, b, c]` with `a + b + c == 0`. Each triplet must be in ascending order, and the returned list must be sorted in lexicographical order.

title: Valid Sudoku
prompt: Write a Python function `is_valid_sudoku(board: list[list[str]]) -> bool` that returns True if a 9x9 Sudoku board is valid: each row, each column, and each of the nine 3x3 sub-boxes must contain the digits '1'-'9' without repetition. Empty cells are '.' and are ignored. A partially filled board can be valid.
test_cases: b2 = [r[:] for r in valid_board]; b2[0][2] = '5'; assert is_valid_sudoku(b2) == False
b3 = [r[:] for r in valid_board]; b3[1][0] = '5'; assert is_valid_sudoku(b3) == False
b4 = [r[:] for r in valid_board]; b4[1][1] = '5'; assert is_valid_sudoku(b4) == False
assert is_valid_sudoku([['.'] * 9 for _ in range(9)]) == True
b6 = [['.'] * 9 for _ in range(9)]; b6[0][0] = '9'; b6[8][8] = '9'; assert is_valid_sudoku(b6) == True

title: Gas Station Circuit
prompt: Write a Python function `can_complete_circuit(gas: list[int], cost: list[int]) -> int` that returns the starting gas station index from which a car can complete the full circuit, or -1 if it is impossible. The car starts with an empty tank; at station `i` it gains `gas[i]` fuel and spends `cost[i]` fuel to reach station `i+1` (circularly). If a solution exists it is unique.

title: Decode Ways
prompt: Write a Python function `num_decodings(s: str) -> int` that returns the number of ways to decode a non-empty string of digits `s`, where '1' to '26' map to letters 'A' to 'Z'. A '0' cannot be decoded on its own; it is only valid as part of '10' or '20'.

title: Rotting Oranges
prompt: Write a Python function `oranges_rotting(grid: list[list[int]]) -> int` that returns the minimum number of minutes until no cell has a fresh orange. Cells are 0 (empty), 1 (fresh), or 2 (rotten). Every minute, each fresh orange adjacent (4-directional) to a rotten orange becomes rotten. Return -1 if some fresh orange can never rot, and 0 if there are no fresh oranges initially.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
prompt: Write a Python function `longest_consecutive(nums: list[int]) -> int` that returns the length of the longest consecutive integer sequence in `nums`. Return 0 if `nums` is empty.
